relevance_note: The paper describes four individuals with TNFAIP3 variants in two families: 'Four HA20 patients in the two families presented with childhood-onset recurrent oral and genital ulcers'.
method_note: Read the whole paper (main text, Tables 1-2, supplementary Tables S1-S2) by hand; a Python script in my scratch directory only assembled the JSON, built Table 1 spans by copying cells from the Markdown, and checked spans and fields. Table 1 has patients as columns; header row '| Patient | Patient 1 | Patient 2 | Patient 3 | Patient 4 |'. Table 1 '+' cells were read as present; its '–' cells are not defined in the table notes or text, so they were treated as not reported (no exclusions from them). Labels: the paper writes both 'Patient N' and 'patient N' (case only); the Table 1 form 'Patient N' is used. Relatives with pedigree labels (III-1, II-5, II-2 in Fig. 1a) use those labels; note that 'II-2' here is the paternal aunt in family 1, while Patient 4 is II-2 in Fig. 1b. Scope: Patients 1-4 carry TNFAIP3 variants. Affected relatives without genotype (III-1 elder brother, II-5 father, II-2 paternal aunt; family 1) are included. The non-carrier parent of Patient 3 is included as a tested relative ('WES was performed ... on the parents of patient 3'; Patient 4 is the other parent); the paper gives no label, sex or result for this person, so the label is 'parent of Patient 3' and there is no variant row. Excluded as neither tested nor affected: the proband's mother II-6 in family 1 ('had no BD-like symptoms') and maternal relatives I-1, I-2, II-3, II-4 in family 2 ('had no BD-like symptoms'). cohort_size_as_stated = 25 ('Twenty-five patients from 12 families'). Table 2 (54 HA20 cases incl. 50 previously reported [5-15]) and Tables S1/S2 are group-level only and give no rows. The family 2 deletion also includes PERP; it is one variant, recorded once per person under TNFAIP3. Zygosity of the deletion is taken from the authors' statement of TNFAIP3 haploinsufficiency in family 2; maternal inheritance for Patient 3 is recorded because qPCR confirmed the deletion in her mother (Patient 4). Consanguinity 'no' for Patient 2 and III-1 relies on their being siblings of Patient 1, whose parents are non-consanguineous. Patient 3 drug doses ('colchicine (400 mg/day), cimetidine (1.0 mg/day)') are recorded as printed. Possible inconsistencies: (1) Patient 4 has '–' in the Table 1 Fever row and the abstract says recurrent fever attacks in 'three of four patients', but the text says 'She presented fever with tonsillitis and lymphadenitis several times a year since her childhood'; because '–' is undefined and the count names nobody, this is not a formal contradiction and fever/recurrent fever is recorded as observed from the text. (2) Patient 3: an early colonoscopy 'did not identify any abnormality' but later endoscopy at 10 years showed multiple intestinal ulcers; treated as change over time, both rows kept. (3) Patient 1: Table 1 marks genital ulcers '+' while the text mentions 'perianal ulcers'; both recorded. CNS involvement for II-5 is marked observed on the basis of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
